reading.body:
Frank Pallone's AI record shows five committee contributions from Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Intel between March 2025 and May 2026, alongside four recorded votes on AI bills and one cosponsorship.

The contributions repeat. Google gives $2,500 three times, Microsoft $5,000 twice, Amazon $5,000 twice, Intel $2,500 once. The total is $30,000 across five committees in roughly fourteen months. The votes and the cosponsorship run the other direction in time, from April 2025 to July 2026, and every recorded vote in the data is a Yea.

What the data does not contain is any bill text, any committee hearing, or any statement by Pallone about AI. The cosponsorship entry lists twelve bill titles, all child-safety and minor-protection measures, but the data does not say what any of them require of AI developers, data centers, or compute. The contributions are dated before and after the votes, and the page states plainly that placement is not a claim of causation. Nothing here connects to power, buildings, or the grid.

The record covers one member of Congress and thirteen events. It cannot show whether these contributions are typical for a senior House Democrat, whether the AI committees give to many members, or whether the votes would have gone differently without the money. Those comparisons would need other members' pages.
